learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the brilliant political satire on the pride, stubbornness, and eventual downfall of those in power, while exploring the theme of destiny.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: When the Maharaja of Pratibandapuram was born, the chief astrologer predicted that he would grow up to be a great warrior but would ultimately be killed by a tiger, specifically the 100th tiger.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🐅 The Vow of the Tiger King
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The King banned tiger hunting for everyone else in his state and vowed to attend to all other state matters only after killing 100 tigers.
When the tiger population in his own kingdom went extinct (after 70 tigers), the King married a princess from a state with a large tiger population just so he could continue his hunt.

The 100th tiger was secretly arranged from a zoo by the terrified Dewan. The King shot it, but missed. The tiger merely fainted from the sound. The hunters secretly killed it to avoid the King's wrath.

Thinking he had defeated fate, the King bought a poorly carved wooden tiger for his son's birthday. A tiny wooden splinter pierced his right hand, causing a deadly infection that killed him. The 100th tiger (a wooden one) took its revenge.

fun_activity.title: 🎭 The Irony Spotter
fun_activity.instructions: Irony is when the opposite of what is expected happens. The King killed 99 real, dangerous tigers but died because of a fake, wooden toy. Can you think of another funny, ironic situation from a movie or real life?

exam_tips: 📌 This story is a 'satire' on the arrogance of people in power. The King neglected his duties, his subjects, and his family just to prove an astrologer wrong.

📌 Highlight the incident with the British officer: The King refused him permission to hunt tigers or even take a photo with a dead one, risking his kingdom. He saved it by sending diamond rings worth 3 lakh rupees to the officer's wife.
📌 The climax is purely dramatic irony—the readers and the hunters know the 100th tiger survived the King's bullet, but the King dies believing he won.
quick_recap: ⭐ As a 10-day-old baby, the prince supposedly spoke, asking the astrologers to tell him the *manner* of his death.
⭐ The Dewan is a comical character who brings a tiger from the People's Park in Madras and hides it in his house.
⭐ The surgical operation at the end was 'successful' because the prophecy was fulfilled: the Tiger King was dead.
